short_description: Liver disease, ten biochemical assays (ALT, A2-macroglobulin, apolipoprotein A-1, total bilirubin, GGT, haptoglobin, AST, glucose, total cholesterol and triglycerides) utilizing serum, prognostic algorithm reported as quantitative scores for fibrosis, steatosis and alcoholic steatohepatitis (ASH)
lay_term: The lab analyst performs the technical lab tests for 10 biochemical assays and carries out an algorithmic analysis using patient data and the lab test results to report a quantitative score for liver fibrosis, steatosis, and alcoholic steatohepatitis (ASH). Explanation The lab analyst performs 10 lab tests for different analytes in a specimen such as blood: 84460 for alanine amino transferase (ALT), 82172 for apolipoprotein A–1, 83883 for A2–macroglobulin, 82247 for total bilirubin, 82977 for gamma glutamyltransferase (GGT), 83010 for haptoglobin, 84450 for aspartate amino transferase (AST), 82947 for glucose, 82465 for total cholesterol, and 84478 for triglycerides. The lab analyst then inputs the test results into a computer program to analyze the data using a specific algorithm, then reports a quantitative score for liver fibrosis, steatosis (fatty liver), and alcoholic steatohepatitis (ASH). Each multianalyte assay with algorithmic analysis (MAAA) test, including 0002M, involves all analytical services to produce test results that become the raw data for the algorithmic analysis. These technical lab services may include laboratory chemical analyses, gene expression profiling using methods such as real time polymerase chain reaction (RT–PCR); fluorescence in situ hybridization (FISH); and molecular pathology tests including steps such as cell lysis, extraction, amplification, and hybridization or detection. It also includes gathering relevant patient data, carrying out the algorithmic analysis, and reporting the results. Although not limited to testing for a specific condition, clinicians may order this blood test to help assess liver status in patients diagnosed with alcoholic liver disease. Terminology Algorithm: A specific set of step–by–step calculations using defined inputs at each step to produce a useful output; for multianalyte assays with algorithmic analyses (MAAA), the output involves some sort of diagnostic or prognostic information about treatment options or disease outcomes. Amplification: Making more copies of a desired gene for study by processes such as polymerase chain reaction (PCR) or transcription of DNA to RNA and reverse transcription from RNA to make an additional copy of the DNA.

short_description: Scoliosis, DNA analysis of 53 single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs), using saliva, prognostic algorithm reported as a risk score
lay_term: The lab analyst performs the technical lab tests for DNA analysis of 53 single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs), and carries out an algorithmic analysis using patient data and the lab test results to report a progression risk score. Explanation The lab analyst performs the lab tests using a specimen such as saliva to analyze 53 genetic markers, which are single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) that have been identified as influencing scoliosis progression. The procedure may involve probes with nucleotide sequences of the 53 target SNPs labeled with fluorescent dye. The SNPS hybridize with the patient specimen, and a detection system evaluates the fluorescence for each probe and reports the presence of each SNP in the patient specimen. The lab analyst inputs the test results along with patient information into a computer program to analyze the data using a specific algorithm, and reports risk–of–progression score indicating the likelihood that the patient’s scoliosis will progress to severe curvature. Each multianalyte assay with algorithmic analysis (MAAA) test, including 0004M, involves all analytical services to produce test results that become the raw data for the algorithmic analysis. It also includes gathering relevant patient data, carrying out the algorithmic analysis, and reporting the results. Although not limited to testing for a specific condition, clinicians may order this test for patients with adolescent idiopathic scoliosis to help assess the likelihood that the condition will progress to severe curvature and thus impact treatment plans. short_description: Oncology (central nervous system), analysis of 30000 DNA methylation loci by methylation array, utilizing DNA extracted from tumor tissue, diagnostic algorithm reported as probability of matching a reference tumor subclass
lay_term: This is an administrative multianalyte assay with algorithmic analysis (MAAA) code represented by a proprietary name in the CPT® MAAA code appendix, meaning that the code applies to only one unique lab test made by a specific manufacturer or performed by a specific lab. Report 0020M only for Epignostix CNS Tumor Methylation Classifier from Heidelberg Epignostix GmbH. The test analyzes 30,000 DNA methylation loci in tumor tissue from the central nervous system (CNS) using a methylation array to detect specific patterns of DNA methylation. The purpose is to compare these patterns against reference tumor subclasses to aid in diagnosing the specific type of CNS tumor. Results are reported as the probability of the sample matching a known reference tumor subclass, facilitating targeted therapeutic strategies. Explanation In this oncology test for central nervous system tumors, the lab analyst performs a detailed analysis using a methylation array, a tool that assesses specific sites of DNA methylation across 30,000 loci. DNA methylation is a biochemical process that adds a methyl group to DNA, typically acting to regulate gene expression and affecting tumor behavior. The DNA used in this test is extracted from tumor tissue previously collected from the patient. The analyst loads the extracted DNA onto a methylation array designed to probe and measure the methylation status at tens of thousands of specific loci in the genome. This data is then processed using a diagnostic algorithm to compare the methylation patterns observed in the tumor DNA with those from known tumor subclasses. This comparison helps to identify which subclass the tumor most closely resembles, based on its methylation profile. This is a multianalyte assay with algorithmic analysis (MAAA), which includes the analytical services to produce test results and uses those results as raw data for an algorithmic analysis that reports the findings as a probability or risk score. For this test, the final report expresses the results as a probability score, indicating how likely the tumor belongs to each reference subclass. Clinicians may use the test to better understand the tumor’s characteristics, potentially guiding more accurate and effective treatment decisions.
